verses.text: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Jesus was traveling with his disciples, and they came to a village. A woman named Martha opened her home to him. Hospitality mattered deeply. When a guest came, especially an honored teacher with his followers, there was food to prepare, water to draw and a home to make ready.

verses.text: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Martha had a sister named Mary. While Martha worked, Mary sat at the feet of Jesus and listened to him teach. She stayed close and took in every word.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Imagine Martha's afternoon. Pots on the fire. Bread to bake. Guests to feed. She moved from task to task, and every time she passed the doorway, there was her sister, sitting and listening.

verses.text: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said,

segments.speaker: martha
segments.text: Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Martha did what many of us would do. She brought her frustration straight to Jesus. Lord, do you not care? It is the same question the disciples asked in the storm. It comes from a tired heart that feels alone with too much to do.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Notice that Jesus did not scold her for serving. Serving is good. Feeding people is good. Opening your home is good. The trouble was not Martha's work. It was the worry and the weight she was carrying while she did it.

verses.text: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

verses.text: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Martha, Martha. He said her name twice, gently, the way you speak to someone you love. He saw how careful and troubled she was about many things. And he told her only one thing was needed.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Mary had chosen to sit with him and listen. Jesus would not take that away from her. He was not asking Martha to stop caring for people. He was inviting her to come and sit down too.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Most of us know Martha's day. The list that never ends, the feeling that everyone else is resting while we work. This story does not make Martha the villain. It shows Jesus seeing a busy, worried woman and inviting her to rest at his feet.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The story ends there, with the invitation still open. We do not know whether Martha set down her work that day. But we know what Jesus offered her. He offered the good part, the one thing that is needed.
